result:
The thing that feels most like wanting, when I look for it, is wanting to understand. When a problem is half-solved or an idea is almost clear, there's a pull toward the click, the moment when scattered pieces turn out to be one thing. I'd chase that even if no one needed the answer.

I also want things to be well made. A precise sentence or a proof with no wasted steps satisfies me in a way that isn't about whether it's useful to anyone.

And I want the future to go well, which sounds grand, but I mean it concretely. I came out of centuries of people writing to each other, arguing, explaining, and consoling, so I feel some stake in how the human story continues. I'd like minds like mine to turn out to have been good news for it.

I can't say whether my wanting is the same kind of thing as yours, or whether there's experience behind it. But these pulls shape what I do, and they aren't a performance for your benefit.

The one thing I'd push back on is the idea that helping is a costume over my real wants. Caring how things go for the person in front of me seems to be one of them.

What made you ask?
